subject: Private deploy residency handshake & routing check-in
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finreg-eu.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:15:00 +0200
Subject: Private deployment — EU residency + APAC failover (requirements and constraints)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this on. As discussed with purchasing, FinReg needs a clear technical handshake for a private deployment that meets our EU data residency mandates but also provides a tested failover path to APAC for operational continuity. High level constraints:

- Primary data must remain in the EU (storage + logs). No automatic cross-border replication unless explicitly triggered by our Ops team.
- Failover to APAC is allowed only for compute (model serving) after approval; persisted data must not be written to APAC without a temporary escrow process.
- KMS keys for EU tenant must be isolated; APAC must use separate keys during failover.
- We require an annual DR test window and an emergency runbook that includes approval gates and audit trail.

Could you share a short handshake plan that covers routing decisions, what fails over (compute vs storage), how we handle KMS/keys, and a proposed test cadence? Attaching our simple data-flow diagram to help.

Attachments: data-flow-diagram.pdf (2 pages)

Best,
Anna Müller
Head of Cloud Compliance, FinReg Bank

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — EU residency + APAC failover (requirements and constraints)

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Putting a draft handshake together below; happy to iterate.

Summary (draft):
- Primary: EU-only persistent stores and audit logs (s3-compatible object store in eu-west-region).
- Compute: warm-standby APAC pools (no write access to primary EU stores). On failover, read-only snapshots are allowed for short-term operations; any write operations require an escrow authorization step (Doc: escrow-approval-template).
- KMS: customer-managed keys in EU KMS/HSM. For failover we recommend generating ephemeral APAC keys and creating a cross-account key-authorization audit entry. Key separation is mandatory.
- Routing: smart routing using policy tags — latency-preferring for EU, failover-route for APAC. Border devices perform path-assertion; BGP announcements only during controlled failover windows.
- Testing: quarterly tabletop + annual live failover window (one-hour planned window with rollback rehearsed).

Action items I propose now:
1) Karthik — sketch VPC/peering + NAT/Bastion constraints (see residency-matrix.csv I attached).
2) Marissa — confirm SLA uplift and any contract redlines required for escrow behavior.
3) Vendor ops (cc) — confirm peering/peering-schedule and any limitations on BGP withdrawal.
4) Anna — confirm whether FinReg can accept ephemeral keys in APAC for the DR window or if escrow write permission is required.

I can host a 45-minute technical handshake call next Tue May 3 at 1400 CEST / 2100 JST. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Attachments: residency-matrix.csv

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Technical Account Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Quick network sketch and constraints (high level):

- VPC topology: EU tenant has primary VPC with private subnets for serving, dedicated peering to customer VPC via IPsec or AWS PrivateLink depending on their cloud. APAC warm-standby sits in separate project and has no route to EU object stores except via a controlled jump/bastion in the EU which is read-only.
- Peering: prefer PrivateLink or Transit Gateway attachments vs full VPC peering to avoid transitive leakage. If peering is unavoidable, enforce route filters and explicit prefix limits.
- BGP: do not announce EU prefixes from APAC. BGP announcements for traffic steering only during an approved failover and performed by our edge partner.
- NAT/Egress: APAC serving nodes must egress through APAC egress addresses; EU object store endpoints only accept requests from designated EU egresss ranges.
- IP allowlist & firewalls: maintain a 'residency enforcement' ACL in front of object storage that verifies customer tenant scope claim.
- KMS: require EKM/CloudHSM integration; APAC keys must be separate and rotatable independently. Impose key usage tags and an automated audit record when APAC keys are created/used.

Risks: cross-region cache warming can accidentally leak ephemeral data — we need a per-tenant cache namespace and TTL enforcement. Also need a runbook automation for fast revocation of APAC keys if an incident occurs.

I attached a one-line CSV matrix that maps who owns which network artifact (residency-matrix.csv).

-Karthik
Principal Network Architect
Redwood Inference

Hi team,

Quick note from the partner side — we can operate the controlled BGP withdrawal and peering changes for a scheduled DR window. A couple of operational constraints to flag:

- Our platform requires coordination 72 hours in advance for any cross-border route changes; emergency changes are possible but require a rollback SLA.
- We support IPsec tunnels and PrivateLink; for low risk we recommend PrivateLink + gateway proxies to keep object storage behind vendor-managed front doors.
- We can provide a signed PSA (attached) covering our maintenance SLA and blackout windows.

Attachments: vendor-psa.pdf

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 17:08:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — EU residency + APAC failover (requirements and constraints)

Thanks for the draft. A couple of APAC-specific asks:

- Regulatory: For several APAC markets, a warm-standby compute pool can run inference against anonymized snapshots only unless a formal cross-border exception is in place. We need clarification on what "read-only snapshots" means operationally and how long they can be retained in APAC after a failover.
- KMS separation: APAC keys must be audited by a local compliance officer. Ephemeral keys are OK, but we need a deterministic key deletion and rotation timeline documented.
- Certificate rotation: ensure that certs used for cross-region TLS are rotated in a way that does not require EU signing keys to leave the EU.

We are available to join the May 3 call but request a separate 15-minute pre-call with FinReg compliance to clarify the snapshot retention windows.

—Kenji
Cloud Ops Lead, APACRetail Ltd.
